Chain hook \u00b7 left.purpose: Take the chain load on a curved steel seat.
Chain hook \u00b7 left.rationale: Two seats share the load along the crosspiece. The contact solver uses gated point constraints at these throat centers.
Chain hook \u00b7 left.basis: P4 preliminary stock. Hook gates and compliant tread are idealized in the physics model.

Hook keeper \u00b7 left.purpose: Close the hook throat once the chain is seated.
Hook keeper \u00b7 left.rationale: Passive keeper envelope. Gate strength, approach and spring travel need verification.
Hook keeper \u00b7 left.basis: P4 preliminary stock. Hook gates and compliant tread are idealized in the physics model.

Compliant belt tread \u00b7 left.purpose: Compress against the NOTE to apply traction in either direction.
Compliant belt tread \u00b7 left.rationale: Six millimeters of soft tread added to the existing belt. Mass, stiffness and installed rotating inertia require measurement.
Compliant belt tread \u00b7 left.basis: P4 preliminary stock. Hook gates and compliant tread are idealized in the physics model.

Lid post 330 \u00b7 right.purpose: Support the keeper rails from the side beam.
Lid post 330 \u00b7 right.rationale: The post carries NOTE contact into the cassette instead of the thin panel edge.
Lid post 330 \u00b7 right.basis: P4 preliminary stock. Hook gates and compliant tread are idealized in the physics model.

Climb yoke post \u00b7 right.purpose: Carry the chain reaction into the cassette side beam.
